articles.headline: Strategic investors and PEs eye BluPine at $2 billion valuation
articles.summary: Multiple private equity firms including KKR, NIIF, and Blackstone are interested in acquiring Actis-owned renewable energy platform BluPine. Actis seeks a valuation between $1.5 billion and $2 billion for the firm, which targets 4GW capacity. Strategic interest also comes from RPSG Group and Torrent Power, with binding bids for the Gurugram-based firm expected within the next two weeks.

articles.headline: Banks vexed by RBI's abrupt end to FCNR deposit scheme
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has surprised lenders by moving the closure of its foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) scheme to 31 August from 30 September. The early termination has created liquidity management challenges for banks that had arranged funding based on the original timeline. The special window had already mobilized $52.3 billion in deposits as of mid-August.

articles.headline: NSE begins IPO valuation process with shares priced at ₹2,500-2,800
articles.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) has completed IPO roadshows, with institutional demand expected to price shares between ₹2,500 and ₹2,800. The exchange has reportedly secured $1 billion in commitments from global investors like JPMorgan and Nomura. The IPO, which could launch by mid-September, marks the culmination of a decade-long plan for the country's largest bourse to go public.

articles.headline: Investigation continues into Air India Phuket-Delhi flight altitude loss incident
articles.summary: Experts are examining the 4 August Air India flight from Phuket to Delhi which suddenly lost altitude, injuring 24 people. Initial reports indicate a failure in all three hydraulic systems of the Airbus A320. While a pilot tested positive for a banned substance, associations claim the technical fault was independent. A preliminary report on the emergency handling is expected within 30 days.

articles.headline: India Inc quarterly profits defy expectations with broad-based growth
articles.summary: Corporate results for the April-June quarter have exceeded analyst predictions despite global tensions. Nifty 50 companies recorded 18% year-on-year profit growth, the highest in 10 quarters. Mid- and small-cap firms performed even better, with 19 sectors beating projections. Strong earnings are providing support to the Indian stock market amid geopolitical risks and fuel price volatility.

articles.headline: Consumption-linked sectors lead FPI inflows in Indian equities for July
articles.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) accelerated their return to Indian markets in July. Consumer services ($1.06 billion), healthcare ($0.81 billion), and consumer durables ($0.77 billion) attracted the strongest inflows. Conversely, capital goods and telecommunications saw net withdrawals. The recovery extends a trend that began in June following a prolonged period of foreign selling.

articles.headline: Private funding via OGQ surpasses government spending for Indian athletes
articles.summary: Olympic Gold Quest (OGQ), a private non-profit, spent ₹77 crore on athlete support in 2024-25, exceeding the ₹34.8 crore spent by the government's TOPS scheme. OGQ supports 178 senior athletes and 111 para-athletes with coaching and equipment. The foundation's donor count has doubled in five years, highlighting the growing role of private enterprise in India’s sporting performance.

articles.headline: Crude oil stays above $90 as US-Iran deal hopes fade
articles.summary: Global crude oil prices remained above $90 a barrel on Tuesday amid choppy trade. Brent futures touched $91.74, the highest since June, as fading hopes of a deal between the US and Iran kept geopolitical risks elevated. Ongoing tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, which handles 20% of global oil trade, continue to stoke supply disruption fears and global inflation concerns.

articles.headline: High Court admits Qatar Holding plea to enforce award against Byju's
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has admitted a petition by Qatar Holding LLC to enforce a SGD 7.2 million arbitration award against Byju Raveendran and Byju's Investments. The fund is also seeking to recover over $235 million in unpaid loans used to acquire Aakash Educational Services shares. The court has issued a notice to the edtech firm and will hear the matter next on 21 September.

articles.headline: Government restricts routine stem cell therapy for microvascular conditions
articles.summary: The health ministry has barred the routine clinical use of stem cell therapy for microvascular diseases like critical limb ischemia and chronic wounds. Such treatments will now only be permitted within authorized research trials. The move follows concerns over rampant unverified commercial practices and lack of certainty regarding clinical benefits for blood flow conditions.

articles.headline: Government frontloads farm spending to mitigate El Niño and monsoon risks
articles.summary: The Centre spent ₹29,593 crore, or 21% of its annual agriculture allocation, in the first quarter of FY27 to support rural incomes. This pace is more than double that of the previous year. The move aims to ensure timely access to subsidized inputs, crop insurance, and credit as El Niño and uneven monsoon patterns threaten agricultural productivity and rural consumption.

articles.headline: India targets tripling piped natural gas connections this fiscal year
articles.summary: The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board aims to add 4 million new piped natural gas (PNG) users this fiscal, up from 1.34 million in FY26. The push comes as the West Asia war strains LPG imports. The government has approved an incentive scheme offering lower-priced domestic gas to city gas distribution companies for every incremental billed domestic connection.

articles.headline: India weighs limited duty-free sugar imports to rein in prices
articles.summary: India is considering measures to bolster sugar supplies and control record prices, including limited duty-free imports and curbs on stocks held by bulk traders. Such imports would be the first in nearly a decade. The potential move follows high benchmark prices in London and New York and aims to stabilize the domestic market during the upcoming festival season.

articles.headline: India initiates WTO consultation with US over quartz product tariffs
articles.summary: India has sought consultations with the United States at the World Trade Organization (WTO) regarding Washington's tariffs on certain quartz products. This adds a new point of trade friction between the two nations as they remain without a formal trade deal. The consultations are proposed to be held virtually, according to a WTO notification dated 14 August.

articles.headline: Uzbekistan keen to import steel from India to reduce logistics costs
articles.summary: Uzbekistan is looking to import steel, including TMT bars, from India to lower costs for the landlocked nation. Uzbekistan currently imports approximately 1 million tonnes of steel annually, primarily from China. The move is viewed as a strategic shift to diversify its supply chain and benefit from competitive Indian pricing in the construction sector.

articles.headline: LinkedIn report shows women underrepresented in global AI job boom
articles.summary: A LinkedIn analysis of 15,000 companies reveals that women hold only 13% of executive positions in the AI industry, compared to 19% in other sectors. Overall, women make up 27% of AI roles. Experts warn that the lack of gender diversity in AI development may reinforce existing inequalities and biases in areas such as hiring, lending, and healthcare.

articles.headline: Government considers acting as anchor customer for domestic chip startups
articles.summary: India may use its buying power and national security requirements to create a market for locally designed semiconductor processors. By specifying India-designed chips for infrastructure like CCTV cameras, the government aims to help startups validate proofs of concept and establish commercial credibility. This comes as domestic firms struggle to move from design to commercial production.

articles.headline: Sony LIV shifts focus to television content as original hits slow
articles.summary: Sony LIV is reducing production of original web shows to focus on star-studded linear TV content and regional language expansion. While franchises like 'Scam' and 'Maharani' will continue, the platform is prioritizing non-fiction hits like 'Kaun Banega Crorepati' and cricket. Parent company Sony Pictures Networks India reported a 15.6% rise in net profit to ₹556.1 crore in FY26.

articles.headline: NeoGeo raises $20 million in Series A for global expansion
articles.summary: Geospatial intelligence startup NeoGeo has secured $20 million in a funding round co-led by Aavishkaar Capital and Neev Fund II. The Gurugram-based company plans to use the capital to open offices in Europe, the Middle East, and the US. NeoGeo provides digital twins and geospatial services for urban governance, cross-country infrastructure, and natural resource management.

articles.headline: RapteeHV in talks to raise $15-20 million for production scale-up
articles.summary: Chennai-based electric motorcycle maker RapteeHV is in talks to raise up to ₹190 crore in a Series A round. The startup aims to increase its manufacturing capacity from 200 to 300 motorcycles per month by January 2027. The new capital will fund retail expansion into cities like Hyderabad, Pune, and Gurugram as it competes with Ola Electric and Ultraviolette.

articles.headline: ReNew reports 16 percent rise in first quarter net profit
articles.summary: ReNew Energy Global Plc reported a net profit of ₹595.3 crore for the June quarter, up from ₹513.1 crore a year ago. Total income grew 16% to ₹4,786.4 crore, supported by module manufacturing and solar sales. The company's portfolio consisted of 20.5GW of renewable capacity as of 30 June. Promoters are currently exploring a proposal to take the Nasdaq-listed company private.

articles.headline: Voltas AC market share improves despite missing first quarter estimates
articles.summary: Voltas reported a 19% rise in operating revenue to ₹4,765 crore for the June quarter, missing analyst estimates. Its AC market share improved to 17.3%, widening its lead over competitors. However, the stock fell 4% as Ebitda margins remained below the long-term target of 7-8% due to high commodity prices, freight costs, and delayed international project execution in West Asia.

articles.headline: Bain Capital seeks bankers for ₹3,000-crore RSB Transmissions IPO
articles.summary: Bain Capital has called for banker pitches for an initial public offering of automotive component maker RSB Transmissions. Pune-based RSB seeks to raise about ₹3,000 crore. Bain holds a 64.3% stake in the company, which recently acquired Setco Auto Systems. RSB specializes in designing components for commercial vehicles and construction equipment for global clients like Tata Motors and JCB.

articles.headline: India's first blue bond sale imminent by state-run maritime lender
articles.summary: Sagarmala Finance Corp and Vadodara Municipal Corp are preparing to launch India's first blue bonds by the end of September. Sagarmala targets raising up to ₹1,000 crore to fund ocean- and water-related projects. Blue bonds are a novel debt instrument used for environmental protection. Globally, over $15 billion in blue bonds have been issued to date.

articles.headline: Disney and ABC sue US regulator over broadcast license reviews
articles.summary: Disney and its ABC unit have sued the US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to block an early review of licenses for eight stations. Disney alleges the Trump administration is retaliating against the network over its news content. The lawsuit, filed in Washington, calls the agency's actions an assault on free speech following repeated threats by President Trump to revoke licenses.

articles.headline: Monsoon rainfall remains 13 percent below average despite July recovery
articles.summary: India's southwest monsoon is 13% below the long-period average as of mid-August. While the deficit narrowed in July, rainfall remains uneven, with 35% of states facing a deficit. Critical rice-growing regions in Bihar and Jharkhand are struggling with deficits of 41% and 21% respectively. Experts expect regional disparities to persist during the rest of the season.

articles.headline: Swiggy shareholders approve cap on foreign ownership at 49.5 percent
articles.summary: Swiggy has received shareholder approval to cap aggregate foreign ownership at 49.5%, enabling it to qualify as an Indian-owned and controlled company. The approval follows a previous rejection in May. Current foreign investors include Prosus, SoftBank, and Tencent. Under Indian rules, domestic entities must hold over 50% beneficial ownership for a firm to be classified as Indian-owned.

articles.headline: Global bond slump drives sovereign borrowing costs to multi-year highs
articles.summary: Longer-maturity government bond yields are surging globally due to inflation angst and geopolitical risks. Yields on 30-year US Treasuries reached their highest since 2007, while French borrowing costs hit 2008 levels. The slump is increasing financing costs for governments, many of whom are shifting debt issuance toward shorter tenors to lock in lower rates amid a challenging fiscal backdrop.

articles.headline: OnePlus raises smartphone prices as memory chip costs soar
articles.summary: Smartphone brand OnePlus has hiked prices for the third time in nine months, with its portfolio now up to 26% more expensive. Memory chip costs have nearly quadrupled in a year, forcing multiple brands to adjust pricing. Simultaneously, the All India Mobile Retailers Association has sought government intervention over OnePlus's alleged shift toward exclusive e-commerce and large retail sales.

articles.headline: Sammaan Capital claims victim status in CBI loan diversion probe
articles.summary: Sammaan Capital (formerly Indiabulls Housing Finance) clarified it is a victim and not an accused in a CBI probe into alleged financial irregularities involving erstwhile promoter Sameer Gehlaut. The Supreme Court has directed the CBI to examine a PIL alleging the diversion of ₹8,000 crore in loans. Sammaan Capital stated that investigative agencies found no wrongdoing by the company itself.

articles.headline: Payouts under ₹25,938 crore PLI Auto scheme to surge in FY27
articles.summary: The Centre expects disbursements under the production-linked incentive scheme for automobiles to more than double to ₹4,700 crore in FY27. Currently, only eight vehicle manufacturers and 10 component makers have products qualifying for incentives. The projected increase reflects the scheme's maturation and strong sales growth in zero-emission vehicles and advanced automotive components.

articles.headline: Apple's anti-AI stance becomes a headache for stock market investors
articles.summary: Apple shares have fallen 10% since 28 July as investors rotate back to AI infrastructure winners like Microsoft and Alphabet. While Apple's decision to avoid the costly AI computing arms race was once seen as a strength, rising memory chip costs and the detachment from the broader tech rally have created concerns. High demand from AI data centers is driving up component prices for Apple devices.

articles.headline: Independent streamers build new Formula 1 fan community in India
articles.summary: In the absence of a traditional TV broadcaster, independent Indian streamers are creating a lucrative creator economy for Formula 1. The F1 fanbase in India has grown to 98 million, driven by short-form content and localized commentary in languages like Hindi and Tamil. Creators are filling a media vacuum, translating technical jargon and drama for a younger, more diverse audience.

articles.headline: Review: Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 delivers functional foldable design
articles.summary: Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold 8 features a redesigned squatter 4:3 aspect ratio for its inner display, priced from ₹1,79,999. The device is thinner and lighter than previous generations, featuring the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 chip. While it lacks a telephoto lens and high-level dust resistance, the rework improves one-handed use and optimizes the screen for video and multitasking.

articles.headline: President Droupadi Murmu Approves Mines and Minerals Development Amendment Bill 2026
articles.summary: President Droupadi Murmu has approved the MMDR Amendment Bill, 2026. The new law creates a uniform financial framework for major minerals and prohibits state governments from imposing additional taxes, royalties, or levies on mineral-bearing land beyond those specified by the Central Government. The law also invalidates certain retrospective mineral-related charges.

articles.headline: Cash in Circulation Growing at Double Digits Despite Digital Payment Surge
articles.summary: RBI Deputy Governor Shirish Chandra Murmu stated that while digital payments are revolutionary, cash in circulation continues to grow at double-digit rates. High cash demand remains prevalent in rural and semi-urban areas and among small businesses. The RBI is exploring substrate coating and polymer notes to increase the durability of low-value currency.

articles.headline: Delhi High Court Restrains Zydus From Selling Cancer Drug Debafenib
articles.summary: The Delhi High Court has prohibited Zydus Lifesciences from manufacturing or selling the cancer drug Debafenib until the patent held by Novartis AG expires in May 2029. The court order, based on a patent infringement plea, is binding on Zydus and its associates. Debafenib is primarily used to treat melanoma and other cancer types.

articles.headline: Tata Motors Plans Rs 40,000 Crore Investment to Boost Production Capacity
articles.summary: Tata Motors aims to invest between Rs 37,500 and Rs 40,000 crore by 2031 to expand its vehicle production. The company plans to increase annual capacity from 9 lakh to 13 lakh units. The investment will focus on electric vehicles, manufacturing infrastructure, and software development, leveraging both internal accruals and external financing.

articles.headline: Indian Aviation Sector Transformation From Government Dominance to Private Strength
articles.summary: Since the 1991 reforms, the Indian aviation sector has evolved into one of the world's fastest-growing markets. The shift from a state monopoly to a competitive landscape saw the rise of private players and the eventual privatization of Air India. Current challenges include high fuel costs, infrastructure gaps, and the need for modern safety regulations.

articles.headline: Reliance Jio Tariff Changes Signal Potential Industry Wide Price Hikes
articles.summary: Reliance Jio has reintroduced Prime Membership fees and modified its entry-level daily data plans, suggesting an imminent tariff increase. Analysts expect average revenue per user (ARPU) to rise as companies seek to justify 5G investments. The move follows similar tariff restructuring by Bharti Airtel, likely pressuring Vodafone Idea to follow suit.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Directs CBI to Probe Suspicious Indiabulls Housing Transactions
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has ordered the CBI to investigate all allegations of suspicious transactions involving Indiabulls Housing Finance and its related entities. The directive follows findings by the Enforcement Directorate. The court reprimanded investigative agencies for their previous inaction regarding these financial irregularities.

articles.headline: Pilots Union Urges DGCA to Increase Random Drug Testing to 25 Percent
articles.summary: The Federation of Indian Pilots (FIP) has requested the DGCA to increase random drug testing for flight crews from the current 10% to 25%. The union argues that the current minimum is insufficient for effective deterrence and safety. They proposed that testing should be truly random and unpredictable throughout the year.

articles.headline: PM Modi to Inaugurate Semicon India 2026 With Global CEOs
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the fifth Semicon India 2026 conference in Delhi on September 17. The event will feature over 290 international companies and 500 exhibitors. PM Modi is expected to meet with global semiconductor CEOs to discuss the progress of the India Semiconductor Mission and commercial production timelines.

articles.headline: Uber and Ixigo Partner to Launch Train Ticket Booking Service
articles.summary: Ride-hailing giant Uber has partnered with travel platform Ixigo to offer train ticket bookings directly through its mobile application. This integration allows users to book tickets, check PNR status, and plan end-to-end travel within a single app. The move aims to expand Uber's presence in the multi-modal transport sector.

articles.headline: Manipal Health Enterprises to Acquire 60 Percent Stake in Dermatuch
articles.summary: Manipal Health Enterprises (MHEL) is set to acquire a 60% stake in premium skincare brand Dermatuch for an enterprise value of Rs 387.5 crore. The acquisition marks Manipal's entry into the digital-first skincare market. The remaining 40% stake will be acquired over the next three years as part of a phased transition.

articles.headline: Dubai Commercial Real Estate Transactions Reach 65 Billion Dirhams in H1
articles.summary: Despite regional conflicts, Dubai's commercial real estate market saw an 8.5% year-on-year increase in transaction value, reaching 65.23 billion dirhams in the first half of 2026. Office space demand drove the growth, with transaction volumes rising 38%. Limited supply in prime business districts has led to significant price increases.

articles.headline: Nifty and Sensex Fall on Rising Bond Yields and Oil Prices
articles.summary: Indian benchmark indices fell for the sixth consecutive session on Tuesday. The Nifty closed at 24,155, down 133 points, while the Sensex dropped 493 points to 77,236. Rising US bond yields (5.32% for 30-year) and Brent crude prices reaching $89.80 dampened global investor sentiment and sparked selling in technology and IT stocks.

articles.headline: BSE Shares Hit Four Month Low Following Multiple Analyst Downgrades
articles.summary: BSE Ltd shares fell 0.7% to close at Rs 3,308, marking their lowest level since April. The decline followed rating downgrades by Jefferies and Huwama Institutional Equities. Analysts cited concerns over the impact of new SEBI regulations and increased Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on options trading volumes for the decline.

articles.headline: TCS Focuses on AI Partnership Model and 1 GW Data Capacity
articles.summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is emphasizing a partnership-driven model for AI infrastructure. The company plans to develop over 1 GW of AI data center capacity through its 'Hyper Watt' platform. TCS has partnered with private equity firm TPG for an investment of up to Rs 18,000 crore to scale its AI and cloud service offerings.

articles.headline: Finance Minister Urges Public Sector Banks to Increase Pulses Farming Loans
articles.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman directed public sector banks to significantly increase lending for pulses and oilseeds cultivation. The initiative aims to reduce India's import dependency and promote crop diversification. She also asked banks to launch a month-long 'Banking for Youth' campaign starting October 2 for citizens above 16 years.

articles.headline: Vizhinjam International Port Begins Full Commercial Export Import Operations
articles.summary: Vizhinjam Port in Kerala has officially commenced full export-import operations. The Adani Group-led port can now ship goods to European markets in just 24 days, down from nearly two months. The port's annual capacity is expected to reach 57 lakh TEU by 2028 with a total investment of Rs 30,000 crore, positioning it as a major global transshipment hub.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Forms Committee to Probe Lathicharge During BJP Protests
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has constituted a three-member independent committee to investigate allegations of police brutality during protests by the Chhattisgarh Janata Party. The committee, comprising retired judges and a senior police official, will examine facts regarding the use of force and report back to the court to determine further legal action.

articles.headline: SC Issues Notices on Plea to Seize Assets of Paper Leak Accused
articles.summary: A Supreme Court bench has issued notices to the Centre and State governments on a Public Interest Litigation (PIL) seeking the seizure of assets belonging to individuals involved in exam paper leaks. The plea argues that the future of students is at stake and stringent financial penalties, including asset attachment, are necessary to deter organized crime.

articles.headline: OpenAI Launches Teen ChatGPT With Enhanced Safety and Parental Controls
articles.summary: OpenAI has introduced a specialized version of ChatGPT for teenagers aged 13-17. The platform includes automated safety features that filter inappropriate or sexual content and provide parental monitoring tools. The initiative is designed to support academic learning while maintaining strict safety standards tailored for younger users.

articles.headline: Stock Market Update: Indo Count and Paras Defence Hit Record Highs
articles.summary: Indo Count Industries emerged as the top gainer in the BSE A-group, rising 12.5%. Paras Defence and Space Technologies hit a new all-time high of Rs 1,527.7. Netweb Technologies also reached a record peak of Rs 5,398. Conversely, SBI Card and Payment Services was among the top losers, falling 4.6% to hit a 52-week low.

articles.headline: Retired SC judge to lead probe into CJP Parliament march police action
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has appointed a committee, led by a retired SC judge and a retired HC Chief Justice, to investigate allegations of police misconduct during a student protest march on July 20. The panel will probe counter-allegations of unruly behavior by protesters and recommend guidelines for the graded use of force to control future demonstrations.

articles.headline: Centre considers extended trial runs for highways before official inauguration
articles.summary: Following recent incidents of road failures and safety deficiencies on newly built expressways, the Indian government is weighing a proposal to conduct mandatory extended trial runs. These trials would last several months to identify potential construction flaws like cracks or potholes before the infrastructure is formally opened to the public.

articles.headline: Supreme Court to decide on legality of police facial recognition systems
articles.summary: The Supreme Court is set to rule on the constitutionality of the facial recognition system (FRS) used by police. The court will examine if the technology violates the right to privacy and if its use is legally sanctioned. Concerns have been raised over the use of FRS to identify individuals from protest videos and link them to criminal records without proper oversight.

articles.headline: Indian grandmother with US green card detained by ICE
articles.summary: Venkata Vasamsetty, an Indian citizen and grandmother of two who has held a US green card since 2013, was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement in North Carolina. The detention occurred during a targeted deportation drive. Her family claims she has lived in the US legally for 27 years and only briefly returned to India in 2022 for medical care.

articles.headline: High Court sets aside suspension of Karnataka PSC chairman
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court has quashed the Governor's order suspending Shivashankarappa S Sahukar, the chairman of the Karnataka Public Service Commission. The court ruled that the suspension was unsustainable as the Governor did not act on the advice of the council of ministers. Sahukar will be reinstated with all sequential monetary benefits.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu hikes paid maternity leave for third child to one year
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government has announced an increase in paid maternity leave for its employees for their third child. The leave period has been raised from 12 weeks to a full year, matching the benefit provided for the first two children. The move aims to support women in the workforce and improve maternal and infant health outcomes in the state.

articles.headline: ORR companies demand pause on roadworks to prioritize Metro construction
articles.summary: The Outer Ring Road Companies Association (ORRCA) has requested the Bengaluru government to pause road white-topping projects and prioritize the Blue Line Metro construction. The association expressed concern that simultaneous work is causing extreme dust and traffic congestion, impacting thousands of employees. They have urged for a phased approach to infrastructure development.

articles.headline: BTech-MBA graduate arrested for luxury car theft network in Rajasthan
articles.summary: Bengaluru police have arrested a highly educated thief, holding BTech and MBA degrees, for operating an interstate luxury car theft ring. The accused used sophisticated gadgets to bypass security systems and duplicate keys. Stolen vehicles were reportedly transported to the India-Pakistan border region in Rajasthan to be sold at low prices to criminal networks.

articles.headline: Bengaluru local bodies on alert over mass exclusion from voter lists
articles.summary: Political parties and city officials are concerned after data revealed that nearly 45% of Bengaluru's electoral rolls are under review for potential exclusion. Over 46.8 lakh voters have been flagged under 'Absent, Shifted, Dead, Duplicate' categories. Authorities are conducting door-to-door verification to ensure genuine voters are not disenfranchised during the revision process.

articles.headline: Opposition disrupts Karnataka Assembly over cleansing resolution and scam
articles.summary: For the second consecutive day, opposition parties in the Karnataka Assembly blocked a resolution and disrupted proceedings. The protest was triggered by a controversial ritual performed at a public site and ongoing allegations regarding a multi-crore scam. Opposition leaders have demanded the immediate resignation of the minister involved in the alleged financial irregularities.

articles.headline: Mallikarjun Kharge dares BJP to file case against Nehru and Gandhi
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge has challenged the BJP to file cases against national icons Mahatma Gandhi, Jawaharlal Nehru, and Sardar Patel if they consider singing only two stanzas of Vande Mataram a crime. This follows BJP criticism of a Congress event where the full song was not sung. Kharge accused the ruling party of trying to distort India's freedom struggle history.

articles.headline: Digantara building satellite system to track space debris and objects
articles.summary: Bengaluru-based space-tech firm Digantara is developing a network of ground-based optical sensors and satellites to monitor objects in Earth's orbit. The system, called MOSAIC, aims to provide real-time tracking of space debris and foreign satellites to safeguard India's space assets. The first deployment of five sensor nodes will focus on Low Earth Orbit surveillance.

articles.headline: PM CARES Fund audit reveals balance of 8,452 crore rupees
articles.summary: The latest audit of the Prime Minister’s Citizen Assistance and Relief in Emergency Situations (PM CARES) Fund shows a closing balance of ₹8,452 crore for the fiscal year ending March 2026. The fund, established to deal with public health emergencies like the Covid-19 pandemic, consists entirely of voluntary contributions from individuals and organizations.

articles.headline: Delhi makes third language and vocational education mandatory for Class IX
articles.summary: The Delhi government has introduced a new three-language formula and mandatory vocational education for Class IX students under the revised CBSE plan. Students will now have to study three languages, with at least two being native Indian languages. The move aims to promote multilingualism and skill development from a younger age in alignment with the National Education Policy.

articles.headline: Swiggy investors approve higher foreign ownership cap for IPO
articles.summary: Shareholders of Swiggy have approved a proposal to raise the limit for foreign investment in the company. The move is seen as a crucial step ahead of its planned initial public offering (IPO). The approval allows Swiggy more flexibility to attract international capital while maintaining its status as an Indian-owned and controlled entity under current foreign exchange laws.

articles.headline: Indian scientists develop cancer drug candidate for Mayo Clinic
articles.summary: A team of Indian researchers has successfully developed a potential drug candidate that can block a protein responsible for treatment resistance in various cancers. The molecule, which targets the GIPC1 protein, is being evaluated by the Mayo Clinic in the US. If successful, the drug could significantly improve outcomes for patients with pancreatic, gastric, and lung cancers.

articles.headline: Rishabh Pant hits record sixes to put India ahead in Galle
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant scored a century and hit a record 100th six in Test cricket to give India a commanding lead against Sri Lanka on Day 4 of the first Test in Galle. Pant’s aggressive innings helped India set a target of 372 for the hosts. Sri Lanka ended the day at 84/4, needing 288 more runs to win, while Indian bowlers dominated the evening session.

articles.headline: India men's hockey team faces Pakistan in high-stakes Asian clash
articles.summary: The Indian men's hockey team is preparing to face traditional rivals Pakistan in a crucial group-stage match. Following a series of strong performances, India aims to maintain its dominance in the region. The match is expected to be a high-intensity encounter with significant implications for the tournament standings and the psychological edge ahead of the knockouts.

articles.headline: SC agrees to quash FIRs against student NEET protesters
articles.summary: The Supreme Court agreed to invoke Article 142 to quash FIRs against students who protested NEET-UG paper leaks. The court will protect students protesting peacefully but will decide on FIRs involving those with serious criminal antecedents separately. A high-powered panel will examine protest issues, and police use of facial recognition is under scrutiny for proportionality.

articles.headline: President orders inquiry against KPSC chief; HC quashes suspension
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court set aside Governor's order suspending KPSC Chairperson Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar, citing lack of ministerial advice. The court ordered his reinstatement within seven days but barred him from decisions related to his daughters' selection. President Droupadi Murmu has ordered an inquiry into allegations of misbehaviour against Sahukar.

articles.headline: Jharkhand cancels exams, leaves nearly 2,000 employees jobless
articles.summary: The Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC-CGL) and other recruitment exams conducted by TSR Data Processing Private Limited since 2014 were cancelled following week-long protests over paper leaks. This decision affects 1,975 employees who had successfully cleared exams and become government employees, leaving them jobless and contemplating legal action.

articles.headline: Census questionnaire to offer 'no caste' option, seeks parents' details
articles.summary: India's Census 2027 questionnaire, now live in Ladakh and other areas, includes a 'no caste' option and seeks detailed information on parents' religion and place of birth up to the village level. It also introduces new mandatory questions on Aadhaar, mobile, voter ID, and COVID-19 vaccine status. Congress questioned the methodology.

articles.headline: India registers big win over South Africa in cricket
articles.summary: India registered a big win over South Africa in cricket. The details of the match, score, and specific format are on page 18.

articles.headline: KERC drafts new rules for power cut data on bills
articles.summary: Karnataka Electricity Regulatory Commission (KERC) has drafted Electricity Supply Regulations (ESR), 2026, proposing Escoms show power cut frequency and duration on electricity bills and websites. New rules simplify electricity connections, allowing self-certification for loads up to 150 KW and mandatory online applications with Aadhaar-based e-KYC for transparency.

articles.headline: ORR firms express concern over white-topping work in October
articles.summary: The Outer Ring Road Companies Association (ORRCA) expressed “deep disappointment and serious concern” to the Greater Bengaluru Authority over plans to commence white-topping work on ORR in October 2026, with metro construction still incomplete. They oppose work-from-home as a mitigation strategy and demand prior consultation and technical evaluation.

articles.headline: Warner Music Group to open music technology hub in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Warner Music Group (WMG) announced a significant expansion of its Global Tech division, opening a new international technology hub in Bengaluru next month. The hub will drive technical innovation across WMG’s global tech suite, powering initiatives in music distribution, data infrastructure, and products, leveraging AI and emerging technologies.

articles.headline: Civil society groups seek SIR extension, 'no caste' voter option
articles.summary: Civil society organisations in Karnataka urged Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar to extend the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by three months. They demanded that voters categorised as “Shifted” not be deleted but allowed to transfer registration via Form 8, questioning the basis for deletion and insufficient awareness/training for BLOs.

articles.headline: K.R. Market parking overhaul eases traffic but hurts vendors
articles.summary: A revamped smart parking facility at K.R. Market has streamlined vehicle movement, but small vendors outside the market report a significant decline in business. Barricades installed for vehicle entry have displaced vendors, and increased parking fees are affecting footfall. Civic works around the market also contribute to reduced customer traffic.

articles.headline: Uttarahalli-Mysuru Road widening to finish soon via new TDR scheme
articles.summary: Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda announced that the long-pending widening of Uttarahalli Main Road, linking Mysuru Road, will be completed soon. The delay was attributed to lack of interest in the earlier Transferable Development Rights (TDR) scheme; a new scheme has now garnered consent from property owners for land acquisition.

articles.headline: NLSIU V-C denies meeting students on convocation controversy
articles.summary: NLSIU Vice-Chancellor Sudhir Krishnaswamy claimed there was no request from him to meet students regarding the upcoming convocation. This follows an open letter from students and alumni opposing the attendance of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Bar Council of India Chairman Manan Kumar Mishra at the event.

articles.headline: Six arrested in Bengaluru for drug peddling, ₹14.94 lakh seized
articles.summary: Bengaluru police arrested six persons, including three from other States, in separate operations, seizing 25.37 kg of ganja, 20 gms of MDMA, and 7 gms of hydro ganja. The seized narcotic substances have an estimated value of ₹14.94 lakh, and the accused allegedly confessed to procuring and selling them in Bengaluru.

articles.headline: Bengaluru sees spurt in flu-like illness among children; H1N1 confirmed
articles.summary: Paediatricians in Bengaluru are reporting a rise in influenza-like illness, fever, and respiratory infections, especially among school-going children, with some testing positive for H1N1. Doctors advise monitoring severe or prolonged symptoms, hand hygiene, and vaccination for vulnerable groups, noting that cases are rising earlier than usual seasonal patterns.

articles.headline: Over 500 Clarence High School students fall sick; two H1N1 cases
articles.summary: Clarence High School in Bengaluru closed from August 14-18 after over 500 students fell sick with a seasonal flu-like illness and two staff members confirmed H1N1. The Administrator blamed street vendors, but a GBA Health Officer denied the link, attributing it to a contagious common cold and continuing surveillance.

articles.headline: ED raids KPSC, others in veterinary officer recruitment scam
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) raided 21 premises across Karnataka and Ahmedabad, including the KPSC office, Chairperson Shivashankarappa S. Sahukar's residence, and alleged middlemen, in connection with irregularities in the Veterinary Officers' recruitment. The probe examines an alleged money trail, paper leaks, and manipulation of the evaluation process.

articles.headline: Karnataka Commission flags prolonged detention of foreign women inmates
articles.summary: The Karnataka State Commission for Women flagged the prolonged detention of several foreign women inmates at Parappana Agrahara Central Prison, despite their eligibility for release. Many struggle to furnish bail amounts and sureties, especially when courts insist on land or property-based surety. The commission has taken up the matter with the State government.

articles.headline: Ivan D'Souza demands 2% reservation for Christian community
articles.summary: Legislative Council member Ivan D’Souza demanded the creation of a separate sub-category for the Christian community with 2% reservation within the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category. He argued that Christians are unable to obtain adequate benefits through the existing system and urged similar provisions to those for the Muslim minority.

articles.headline: Woman, friend arrested for smothering husband and son in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Bengaluru police arrested Kusuma alias Harini (25) and Vinay Kumar (30) for allegedly murdering her husband Abhinandan (34) and their 4-year-old son in Chikkabanavara. The duo allegedly smothered them, attempting to make the deaths appear as a cardiac arrest. The woman had an alleged relationship with Kumar.

articles.headline: No need to cross-examine Renukaswamy's mother in Darshan case: HC
articles.summary: The Karnataka High Court upheld a trial court’s order, ruling that Renukaswamy’s mother’s answers during cross-examination by the defence in actor Darshan's murder case do not warrant her cross-examination by the prosecution under Section 154 of the Evidence Act, as she has not turned hostile or disowned the prosecution case.

articles.headline: Students propose innovative snakebite solutions at innovation challenge
articles.summary: College students at the Nagathon Snakebite Innovation Challenge presented innovative solutions, including a cloud-based dashboard for antivenom location, an AI-assisted network for immediate first-aid guidance, and a community behavior-change campaign focused on reducing delays in seeking medical care. Team NAGAM won the first prize of ₹1.5 lakh.

articles.headline: Tusker Abhimanyu retires from Mysuru Dasara duties at 60
articles.summary: Abhimanyu, the celebrated lead elephant of the Mysuru Dasara jumbo squad, has officially retired from annual festivities after attaining 60 years of age in April. Despite initial inclusion, the Forest Department decided to relieve him, acknowledging his impeccable record as the lead elephant but prioritizing age-related guidelines.

articles.headline: Congress terms BJP 'anti-Dalit' over 'purification' row, protest
articles.summary: The Congress accused the BJP of being 'anti-Dalit' for blocking a unanimous resolution condemning the 'purification' ceremony in Uttarakhand after Mallikarjun Kharge's rally. BJP and JD(S) continued protests in the Assembly, demanding Minister B. Nagendra's resignation over alleged fund misuse and a chargesheeted case, leading to legislative stalemate.

articles.headline: Mankal Vaidya elected unopposed as Karnataka Dy. Speaker
articles.summary: Two-time MLA Mankal Vaidya of the Congress was unanimously elected as Deputy Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly. The opposition BJP facilitated the unopposed election by boycotting, while Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar congratulated Vaidya, who comes from the fishing community.

articles.headline: Umashree elected Dy. Chairperson, recalls life struggles
articles.summary: Veteran actor and former Minister Umashree was unanimously elected Deputy Chairperson of the Legislative Council. In an emotional speech, she recalled her early-life struggles as a single mother of two and how social work helped her overcome pain and loneliness. She thanked her family and supporters for her political journey.

articles.headline: Demand for greater SC/ST inclusion in cooperative sector
articles.summary: Legislative Council member K. Shivakumar demanded increased participation of Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in Karnataka's cooperative sector. He highlighted disparities in loan disbursement (only ₹3,094 crore out of ₹5,980 crore disbursed) and membership, urging the government to ensure reservation policy compliance and provide more employment opportunities.

articles.headline: CM DKS vows to work with all parties for Karnataka's development
articles.summary: Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar affirmed he would not use his office to make enemies or hurt anyone, vowing to work with leaders of all political parties for Karnataka's development. He also announced his attendance at the Southern States Chief Ministers’ Conference, where the Cauvery water-sharing issue is expected to be a key discussion.

articles.headline: JD(S) demands Karnataka government drop Bidadi Township project
articles.summary: JD(S) supremo H.D. Deve Gowda demanded the Karnataka government drop the Bidadi Township project, arguing it would deprive small farmers of their livelihoods. He, along with H.D. Kumaraswamy and Nikhil Kumaraswamy, criticized the Congress for reviving the project and challenged CM Shivakumar to an open debate on the NICE Road project.

articles.headline: CM Shivakumar tells T.N. leaders not to interfere in Hanur case
articles.summary: Karnataka CM D.K. Shivakumar asked Tamil Nadu politicians not to interfere in the Hanur case, where three suspected poachers were killed in a shootout with forest personnel. He stated, 'This is a federal structure. No State should interfere with another State’s administration. We know how to protect our State.'

articles.headline: Forest Dept. lodges complaint over attack on anti-poaching camps
articles.summary: Forest Department officials lodged a complaint with the police over attacks on anti-poaching camps and residential quarters in the Cauvery Wildlife Sanctuary near Hanur. The attacks followed the killing of three suspected poachers in an alleged exchange of fire with forest personnel. Police denied protestors triggered blasts.

articles.headline: Former BJP Minister B.C. Nagesh passes away at 65
articles.summary: Former Karnataka Minister B.C. Nagesh (65) of the BJP passed away in Bengaluru after a brief illness. A two-time MLA from Tiptur, he served as Minister for School Education and Literacy and was known for his pro-people stances, despite a controversial tenure with textbook revisions.

articles.headline: Karnataka forms sub-committee to vet revised minimum wages
articles.summary: The Karnataka government announced a Cabinet sub-committee, headed by Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara, to review the revision of minimum wages. While labour unions welcomed the increase, industries have opposed it, stating the hike is too steep and could deter investments. The committee will assess consonance with the Code on Wages, 2019.

articles.headline: PM CARES Fund donations drop, utilisation abysmal
articles.summary: Audited financial statements for the PM CARES Fund (2023-24 and 2024-25) show donations dropped 30% to ₹480 crore in 2024-25, but the total corpus grew 25.8% to ₹8,453 crore, primarily due to interest earnings. Fund utilisation remained abysmal at ₹87.5 lakh (0.01% of corpus), with refunds from implementing agencies exceeding utilisation.

articles.headline: Sonia Gandhi's memoir 'Belonging' to cover love, loss, political career
articles.summary: Congress leader and Rajya Sabha member Sonia Gandhi’s memoir, 'Belonging: A Journey of Love,' will be published on November 10. The book will reflect on her marriage into the Nehru-Gandhi dynasty, personal tragedies, and her political career, including turning down the Prime Minister's post, offering a unique perspective on India’s social and political changes.

articles.headline: Kharge flags 1.95 lakh blocking orders to social media sites
articles.summary: Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge accused the Modi government of a 'brazen and calculated attack' on democratic rights, alleging it issued 1.95 lakh blocking orders to social media platforms in five months. He claimed this censorship targeted critics, including students protesting exam irregularities, without comparable action against ruling party supporters engaging in online harassment.

articles.headline: Controversial past posts disappear from new BJP social media team's X accounts
articles.summary: Hours after the BJP announced its new national social media team, the X profiles of several office-bearers became unavailable as screenshots of their controversial older posts circulated. Some posts allegedly criticized Congress leaders, reservation, and one user expressed being 'ashamed of her surname,' claiming to be 'a huge fan of Nathuram Godse'.

articles.headline: Calcutta HC refuses to interfere with Ritabrata Banerjee's LoP appointment
articles.summary: The Calcutta High Court refused to interfere with the West Bengal Assembly Speaker’s decision to appoint Ritabrata Banerjee as the Leader of the Opposition. A Division Bench ruled that a Single Bench will have to dispose of the case, filed by Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay, within two months.

articles.headline: Opposition calls SIT report on Ram Temple embezzlement a farce
articles.summary: Opposition parties in Uttar Pradesh, including Congress and Samajwadi Party, described the Special Investigation Team (SIT) report on the Ram Temple embezzlement case as a 'farce' and 'eyewash'. This follows sources indicating a clean chit for the Temple Trust’s former general secretary Champat Rai. They demanded the report be made public.

articles.headline: BRICS calls EU’s carbon tax ‘punitive, unilateral’
articles.summary: BRICS countries on Tuesday opposed the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms (CBAMs), describing them as 'unilateral, punitive, discriminatory and protectionist' climate measures. They urged developed nations to honour financial commitments agreed at the 2025 UN climate conference and significantly increase adaptation finance to help developing countries.

articles.headline: BJP appoints Vinod Tawde, Satish Poonia as State in-charges
articles.summary: BJP president Nitin Nabin appointed Rajya Sabha member Vinod Tawde as the party’s in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, Satish Poonia for Punjab, and Tarun Chugh for Gujarat. These appointments are made with an eye on the Assembly elections in 2027 for UP and Punjab, and later in Gujarat.

articles.headline: H1N1 cases rising across States, experts advise caution
articles.summary: Several Indian States are reporting a spike in H1N1 cases and other influenza-like illnesses, with Delhi recording over 1,300 infections this monsoon season. Experts advise caution, especially for vulnerable groups like children and older adults, and recommend early testing for severe symptoms, but state there is no cause for alarm yet.

articles.headline: SC dismisses plea seeking alternative to execution by hanging
articles.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed a plea to direct the government to find an alternative to execution by hanging. The court cited the absence of botched executions in India and the history of failures with methods like lethal injection in the U.S. It clarified, however, that the ruling doesn't preclude future constitutional scrutiny if new evidence emerges.

articles.headline: Goa moves SC to enhance Tarun Tejpal's rape case sentence
articles.summary: The State of Goa moved the Supreme Court challenging the quantum of sentence given to former Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal in a 2013 rape case. Goa argues that the 10-year prison sentence pronounced by the Bombay High Court was 'grossly disproportionate' to the nature and gravity of the offenses.

articles.headline: Govt. to procure 405 key defence items locally
articles.summary: The Department of Defence Production (DDP) notified its sixth Positive Indigenisation List, comprising 405 strategically important defence items, with an estimated business potential of ₹3,070 crore. This initiative aims to reduce dependence on imports and promote domestic defence manufacturing, including items for the Indian Coast Guard and DPSUs.

articles.headline: Eight labourers killed in M.P. truck-dumper collision
articles.summary: Eight labourers were killed and 32 injured after their pickup vehicle collided with a dumper truck in Madhya Pradesh’s Bhind district early on Tuesday. The accident occurred around 1 a.m. on the Bhind-Gwalior National Highway, with preliminary investigations suggesting the driver lost control while trying to avoid cattle.

articles.headline: Goa nightclub blaze: High Court cancels owners' bail
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday cancelled the bail granted to the owners and a business partner of Birch by Romeo Lane nightclub in Goa. A fire on December 6, 2025, had killed 25 people and injured 50 at the Arpora nightclub.

articles.headline: Škoda Auto India unveils new Slavia sedan, pre-bookings open
articles.summary: Škoda Auto India unveiled its new Slavia sedan, with pre-bookings starting Tuesday at ₹15,000. Prices will be announced later, and deliveries are expected from the beginning of the festive season. The company also announced the introduction of its top-of-the-line sedans, Octavia RS and the all-new Superb.

articles.headline: BSE shares decline for fifth session after Jefferies downgrade
articles.summary: Shares of Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) Ltd. fell for a fifth straight session, closing down 0.7% at ₹3,308 a piece. This follows a downgrade by brokerage Jefferies to 'underperform,' citing headwinds from an STT hike, RBI bank guarantee norms, and Closing Auction Session (CAS) issues, cutting FY27-29e EPS by 5-12%.

articles.headline: Meta faces 29-state trial over social media's youth mental health impact
articles.summary: A coalition of 29 U.S. states began a trial against Meta Platforms, alleging Instagram and Facebook were designed to harm young users' mental health and improperly collected children’s personal data. The trial, potentially reshaping the apps, will see Meta founder Mark Zuckerberg testify. Meta claims efforts to keep kids safe online.

articles.headline: Govt. to allot more APM natural gas for domestic PNG
articles.summary: The Centre announced that eligible city-gas distributors (CGDs) would be allocated an additional 200 standard cubic metre (SCM) of lower-priced Administered Price Mechanism (APM) natural gas for every incremental billed domestic-PNG connection, effective September 1. This aims to help CGDs offset LNG-sourcing costs and accelerate PNG connections.

articles.headline: Volkswagen Group focuses on India localisation, portfolio expansion
articles.summary: European carmaker Volkswagen Group, with six brands in the Indian market, will focus on enhancing its product portfolio and growing localisation to drive future growth, considering India an 'extremely important and strategic market.' It plans new product introductions and confirms all its products are E20 compliance compatible for higher ethanol blending.

articles.headline: Erdogan signs law on conditional pardon for disarmed PKK militants
articles.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan signed into law a measure introducing a limited, conditional pardon for thousands of Kurdish militants as part of a government peace effort with the PKK. The law will come into force only after Turkiye’s National Security Council confirms that the group has fully disarmed.

articles.headline: Syria sentences Assad's cousin to death for atrocities
articles.summary: A Syrian court on Tuesday handed a death sentence to Wassim al-Assad, a cousin of long-time ruler Bashar al-Assad, for atrocities committed under the autocrat’s rule. This follows Bashar al-Assad's own death sentence in absentia last week.

articles.headline: U.S. sanctions ICC President Tomoko Akane of Japan
articles.summary: The United States on Tuesday imposed sanctions against International Criminal Court (ICC) President Tomoko Akane of Japan as part of its campaign against the body, which Washington accuses of being 'politicised'. Sanctions were also placed on ICC Senior Trial Lawyer Abdoulaye Seye of Senegal.

articles.headline: Putin hosts Myanmar's leader to deepen cooperation
articles.summary: Russian President Vladimir Putin hosted the head of Myanmar’s military-backed government, Min Aung Hlaing, for talks in Russia on Tuesday, aimed at boosting their cooperation. Putin noted that both countries have cooperated on foreign policy and security issues, indicating a strengthening relationship.

articles.headline: Russian missile strike kills 10 in Ukrainian village
articles.summary: A Russian missile strike on a village in Ukraine’s northeastern Kharkiv region killed at least 10 people and wounded eight others, demolishing homes. This occurred as Ukrainian forces staged one of their biggest drone attacks on Russia, firing almost 800 drones, with Russia intercepting 791 Ukrainian drones overnight.

articles.headline: Bangladesh doesn't want India ties to decline over Teesta
articles.summary: Bangladesh’s Water Resources Minister Shahiduddin Chowdhury Anee stated that Bangladesh does not want its friendly ties with India to deteriorate over the long-pending Teesta water-sharing agreement. He urged New Delhi to take into account Dhaka’s interests while pursuing its own, amidst a renewed push by Bangladesh to address the issue.

articles.headline: UAE accuses Iran of firing two ballistic missiles at its territory
articles.summary: The United Arab Emirates on Tuesday accused Iran of firing two ballistic missiles at its territory. UAE air defences detected the missiles, with the first falling outside and the second within territorial waters. This marks the first such alert since a false alarm in June and targeting of ADNOC tankers.

articles.headline: Hamas committed to Gaza peace deal after Trump envoy talks
articles.summary: Hamas stated on Tuesday it remained committed to the U.S.-backed Gaza peace deal, despite White House envoy Jared Kushner speaking to Israel about steps towards Hamas’s disarmament. Hamas's spokesperson said Israel has not given clear approval of the roadmap. Disarmament is expected to precede Gaza reconstruction.

articles.headline: India needs six wickets on final day to win first Test against Sri Lanka
articles.summary: India closed day four of the first Test against Sri Lanka with the host at 84 for four, chasing a target of 372. India needs six wickets on the final day to secure a victory. Rishabh Pant’s blistering 66 (69b) helped India score 193 in its second innings.

articles.headline: Padikkal stresses importance of grabbing opportunities in Tests
articles.summary: Devdutt Padikkal, after scores of 167 and 44 in the first Test, emphasized the importance of seizing opportunities at the No. 3 slot. He spoke about adapting his technique for red-ball cricket and the enjoyable chemistry with Karnataka-mate K.L. Rahul, highlighting how that helps in stitching partnerships.

articles.headline: Lakshya Sen triumphs in first round of Badminton Worlds
articles.summary: Lakshya Sen overcame a first-game deficit to defeat Austria’s Collins Valentine Filimon 16-21, 21-8, 21-4 in the opening round of the Badminton World Championships. Unnati Hooda also made a winning start to her maiden Worlds with a 22-20, 21-16 win against Thet Htar Thuzar of Myanmar.

articles.headline: Indian mixed doubles pairs eliminated from Badminton Worlds
articles.summary: India's mixed doubles pairs Rohan Kapoor and Gadde Ruthvika, and debutants Ashith Surya and Amrutha Pramuthesh, were eliminated from the Badminton World Championships. Ashith and Amrutha came agonizingly close to an upset against Turkey’s Emre Sonmez and Yasemen Bektas, losing in three close games after squandering match points.

articles.headline: 17 sportspersons named for Arjuna Awards 2025
articles.summary: The National Sports Awards for 2025 were announced, with just 17 sportspersons named for the Arjuna Awards. Awardees include Tejaswin Shankar, Muhammed Ajmal V., and Priyanka Goswami (athletics); Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand (badminton); Vidit Gujarathi and Divya Deshmukh (chess); and Lalremsiami and Rajkumar Pal (hockey).

articles.headline: Karnataka, Chennai stadiums eyed for Duleep Trophy final
articles.summary: The M. Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru and the M.A. Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai are reportedly in the reckoning to host the Duleep Trophy final from September 6 to 10. This move follows BCCI's assurance to conduct the marquee match in front of fans, after earlier rounds at the CoE without spectators.

articles.headline: Football great I. Arumainayagam awarded Arjuna Award (Lifetime)
articles.summary: Indian football great I. Arumainayagam, 86, was conferred the Arjuna Award (Lifetime) 2025. The former speedy winger, who debuted internationally in 1962 and was part of the 1962 Asian Games gold medal-winning team, expressed happiness and pride, stating his family had long awaited this recognition.

articles.headline: R. Praggnanandhaa remains joint second in Sinquefield Cup
articles.summary: R. Praggnanandhaa held top seed Fabiano Caruana to a draw in 56 moves in the seventh round of the Sinquefield Cup, to remain in joint second spot with four points in St. Louis. Wesley So of the United States continues to be in the lead with 4.5 points.

articles.headline: Tanishi Gupta wins 50m butterfly gold at Junior National aquatics
articles.summary: Karnataka's Tanishi Gupta won the girls’ 50m butterfly race, clocking 27.41s, at the 52nd Junior National aquatics championships in Bhubaneswar. Her statemate Charita Panindranath secured the silver medal in the same event, finishing in 27.72s.

articles.headline: Renshaw replaces Weatherald in Australia squad for Bangladesh Test
articles.summary: Australia on Tuesday dropped struggling opener Jake Weatherald and replaced him in the squad with Matthew Renshaw for the second Test against Bangladesh. This change follows Australia's shock home loss in the first Test.

articles.headline: Shereton Anthony's goal helps AIHC Mischievous win hockey title
articles.summary: Shereton Anthony scored the winner as AIHC Mischievous edged out Anglo Sports Club, Trichy, 1-0, to win the senior title at the All India Anglo-Indian Association annual hockey tournament held in Bengaluru on Independence Day.

articles.headline: Chandigarh, Odisha win in Hockey India junior women’s National
articles.summary: Chandigarh defeated Punjab 3-1 in a Division 'A' (Pool-A) match of the 16th Hockey India junior women’s National in Pune. In other results, Odisha beat Bengal 6-0, Manipur edged Maharashtra 3-2, and MP routed Himachal 6-0.

articles.headline: Ashmita Chaliha triumphs at Korea Masters after injury setback
articles.summary: Ashmita Chaliha won her maiden BWF World Tour title at the Korea Masters, fighting back from a game down in the final against Han Qianxi. This victory comes two years after suffering a knee injury in South Korea, overcoming a period of falling rankings and lost sponsorship by adapting her game with more rallies and stamina.

articles.headline: I-T Dept Probes 394 Entities for Suspicious Foreign Remittances
articles.summary: The I-T department, announced by CBDT, is conducting a nationwide probe into 394 entities and 36 professionals for suspicious foreign remittances made over the last three years. Preliminary findings show no correlation between amounts sent and reported turnovers. The investigation focuses on high expenses for freight, software imports, and consulting services not matching business scale, with over 117 entities located in border districts.

articles.headline: Wipro Acquires Majority Stake in Skincare Brand Dermatouch for ₹387.5 Cr
articles.summary: Wipro Consumer Care & Lighting acquired a 60% stake in Ahmedabad-based skincare brand Dermatouch for ₹387.5 crore, with plans to buy the remaining 40% over three years. This marks Wipro's 18th global acquisition, entering India's ₹30,000 crore, 15-16% annual growth premium dermaceutical market. Dermatouch reported a 314% revenue surge in FY25, and Wipro aims to scale its presence in India and internationally.

articles.headline: Ind-Ra Forecasts FY27 GDP Growth at 6.8%; Risks Remain
articles.summary: India Ratings and Research (Ind-Ra) projects India's FY27 GDP growth at 6.8%. Mint and BS state an increase from 6.7% due to lower global crude oil prices, while Hindu notes a slowdown from FY26's 7.6%. Risks include West Asia conflict, El Niño's impact on agriculture, and high fuel and food inflation until late 2026. Ind-Ra assumes oil prices at $85/barrel, with a depreciating currency as a downside risk. RBI projects 6.7%.

articles.headline: Tata Sons AGM Adjourned for First Time Due to Quorum & Trust Issues
articles.summary: Tata Sons' 108th Annual General Meeting was adjourned for the first time in over a century due to a lack of quorum. Key shareholder Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) couldn't nominate a member due to regulatory curbs by the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner amid an ongoing inquiry. This stalled resolutions, including Chairman N. Chandrasekaran's directorship, who later announced he won't seek another term after Feb 2027, with the board approving a successor search.

articles.headline: Gold Prices Surge to Record High of ₹1.58 Lakh Amid Tensions
articles.summary: Gold prices in the national capital surged by ₹2,000 to a record ₹1,58,800 per 10 grams on Tuesday. Silver also advanced ₹730 to ₹2,40,730 per kilogram. The rally was driven by increased festive demand, buying from retailers and stockists, and global supply concerns amid geopolitical tensions and rising crude oil prices. Globally, spot gold hovered around $4,392 per ounce, with domestic sentiment remaining bullish.

articles.headline: Milky Mist Dairy Shares Debut 30% Higher After ₹1,553 Cr IPO
articles.summary: Erode-based Milky Mist Dairy Food Ltd made a strong market debut, with shares closing nearly 30% higher at ₹181.45 against its ₹140 issue price. The ₹1,553 crore IPO, subscribed 56 times, was the largest by an Indian dairy company, giving it a ₹13,968.81 crore market valuation. Singapore sovereign fund Temasek invested ₹482 crore for a 5% stake. The stock debuted at ₹165 on BSE.

articles.headline: Hindustan Copper to Invest ₹7,000 Cr in Major Expansion Plan
articles.summary: State-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) announced a ₹7,000 crore capital investment over the next 5-6 years for exploration, mine expansion, and strategic partnerships. This aims to meet rising domestic copper demand for green energy, infrastructure, and electric transport. HCL added 135.52 million tonnes to its copper ore reserves in the past three years and is pursuing new deposits both in India and overseas.

articles.headline: India's Crude Oil Import Bill Jumps 41% to $13.7 Billion in July
articles.summary: India's crude oil import bill surged 41% year-on-year to $13.7 billion in July, driven by elevated global oil prices and persistent West Asia uncertainty. Import volumes rose 13.3% to 2.14 crore tonnes. Russia remained the top supplier, accounting for 55.5% of total imports. India, heavily dependent on overseas supplies (88.5% of consumption), saw net oil and gas spending rise to $11.2 billion.

articles.headline: NTA Revamps Exam System, Removes 600 Experts After Lapses
articles.summary: The National Testing Agency (NTA) has removed 600 experts and onboarded new ones, revamping its examination process with a four-tier question paper checking system for factual, language, and translation errors. This follows Union Education Minister Pralhad Joshi's directive after NEET-UG and UGC-NET exam lapses. NTA is also filling ten senior leadership roles, including CISO, and overhauling its Confidential Operations architecture to strengthen security.

articles.headline: Trump Cites India's Voter ID System to Advocate US Law
articles.summary: Former US President Donald Trump advocated for a national voter ID law, citing India's election system and remarks by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Trump claimed 646 million Indian voters used valid IDs in the last general election, arguing similar documentation is needed in the US for election integrity. India's Congress party mocked his comments, suggesting he take CEC Kumar and EVMs to America.

articles.headline: Former Delhi Minister Satyendar Jain, 5 Others Arrested in DJB Scam
articles.summary: Former Delhi Water Minister Satyendar Jain and five others, including former DJB CEO Udit Prakash Rai, have been arrested by the Delhi Anti-Corruption Branch (ACB). The arrests are linked to alleged irregularities and a tender scam in augmenting sewage treatment plants, where restrictive specifications reportedly favored Euroteck Environment Pvt. Ltd., involving bribes and embezzlement of public funds. Jain previously served over a year for money laundering.

articles.headline: Counterfeit Drugs Worth ₹5 Crore Seized in Karnataka Racket
articles.summary: The Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration's Enforcement Wing busted a drug racket near Bidadi, seizing counterfeit medicines worth ₹5 crore. Offenders were allegedly manufacturing, repackaging, and labeling cheap, substandard drugs with multinational pharmaceutical company labels to sell to retail pharmacies at high margins. Investigations are ongoing to track the distribution network and address concerns about spurious drugs entering the supply chain.

articles.headline: Pakistan SC Orders Imran Khan Moved to Islamabad Hospital for Check-up
articles.summary: Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered imprisoned former Prime Minister Imran Khan's transfer to a private hospital in Islamabad for a comprehensive medical examination. This follows months of health concerns from his family and personal physicians, who were previously restricted access due to "security threats." The court allowed his family and personal doctor to visit. Khan has been in custody for months following convictions in multiple legal cases.

articles.headline: Krishna Byre Gowda Gets Additional Parliamentary Affairs Portfolio
articles.summary: Krishna Byre Gowda, who holds the Greater Bengaluru Development portfolio, has been given the additional charge of Parliamentary Affairs. This move grants him a bigger role in coordinating legislative business. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar will continue to oversee Law, Justice and Human Rights, which are typically clubbed with Parliamentary Affairs.
